## Beads Issue Tracker

Use Beads (`bd`) for durable task tracking in repositories that include it. Use the `beads` skill (plugin `beads` of the owpac marketplace, installed for both Claude Code and Codex) for Beads workflow guidance, then use the `bd` CLI for issue operations.

### Quick Reference

```bash
bd ready                # Find available work
bd show <id>            # View issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim work
bd close <id>           # Complete work
bd prime                # Refresh Beads context
```

### Rules

- Use `bd` for all task tracking; do not create markdown TODO lists.
- Run `bd prime` when Beads context is missing or stale. Codex 0.129.0+ can load Beads context automatically through native hooks; use `/hooks` to inspect or toggle them.
- Keep persistent project memory in Beads via `bd remember`; do not create ad hoc memory files.

**Architecture in one line:** issues live in a local Dolt DB; sync uses `refs/dolt/data` on your git remote; `.beads/issues.jsonl` is a passive export. See https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/main/docs/core-concepts/sync-concepts.md for details and anti-patterns.

## Tasks and memory (takes precedence over the Beads blocks and `bd prime`)

**Agent names** (Beads actor, engram session ids, provenance `--actor`):
- `claude` when you are Claude Code, `codex` when you are Codex.
- A specialized agent with its own prompt or role is named `claude-<name>` or `codex-<name>` (e.g. `claude-review`). If your prompt states a name, use it.
- `BEADS_ACTOR` is already set to your name (by your tool's config, or by the orchestrator), so `bd` attributes your claims, notes and comments correctly. Never pass a different `--actor`.

**Memory: engram (MCP tools `mem_*`), in every repository.**
- Use engram only when the session does real work: a Beads task, code changes, or an investigation worth remembering. Skip it entirely for quick questions and read-only checks.
- Session start: call `mem_session_start` with:
  - `id`: if your prompt gives you an engram session id, use it verbatim. Otherwise build `<agent>-<beads-id or adhoc>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>`, where `<agent>` is your agent name (see **Agent names** below);
  - `directory` = the current working directory.
  Then call `mem_context` and `mem_search` on the topic at hand.
- Pass that same `session_id` to every `mem_save` and `mem_session_summary`. Without it, engram files everything under a generic session, or rejects the write when several agents run in parallel.
- Durable knowledge (decision, pitfall, discovered convention): `mem_save` with a stable `topic_key` (e.g. `<repo>/<topic>`). Do **not** use `bd remember` or ad hoc memory files, even when Beads instructions say so.
- Session end: `mem_session_summary` (same `session_id`), then `mem_session_end`.
- Do not store anything that can be derived from the code or the git history.

**Tasks: Beads, only in repositories where it is initialized** (`bd prime` context present at session start, or `bd where` succeeds).
- Use `bd ready`, `bd update <id> --claim`, `bd note <id> "…"` for progress, and `bd close`. No markdown TODO lists.
- Reference the Beads ID in related engram memories.
- Your conversation itself is linked to the task automatically: a `PostToolUse` hook (`~/.config/ia/hooks/link-bd-session`) records `<tool>:<session_id>` as a `transcript` provenance, and adds the id to the task metadata `sessions.<tool>`, on every task you claim, note, comment, close or update. Do not record it yourself. The user finds and resumes it with `pac agent task <id>`.
- When you start on a task that earlier sessions already worked on, recover their context first: `bd show <id>` (notes, comments) and `mem_search` on the task id.
- Never run `bd init` or `bd setup` yourself: the user enables Beads with `pac agent init`.

**Never** store patient data, personal data or secrets in engram or Beads.
